newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures rise late to end up sharply.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures rise late to end up sharply.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed sharply higher and near the highs of the session set during a volatile late rally.
Activity was thin and choppy most of the session, with buying surfacing late after prices had languished in a wide range during the late morning and early afternoon.
"This kind of intraday volatility shakes the trees," said Jay Hohmann, stock index futures analyst at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette Securities. "It gets people worried."

S&P futures had come under pressure early, despite gains in the spot index and firmness in other index contracts. A late rally on a large market-on-close buy order Tuesday put futures out of line with the spot index, and selling by a large brokerage house then contributed to pressure in early dealings, traders said.
Selling by a large fund later in the morning kept prices subdued, despite local buying, they said.
Several attempts were made to penetrate resistance near 774.00 in midday trade. The nearby S&P contract finally broke above that level late in the day after bond prices firmed.

Treasury bonds had spent much of the day at steady to lower levels in volatile trade, but after an apparently successful sale of new inflation-indexed notes by the Treasury, bond prices rallied, which in turn lifted stocks.
Technical buying surfaced after the March S&P 500 contract broke above 775.00, which fueled the rally.

However, the premium of the March S&P contract over the index failed widen above the point where arbitrage buy programs would be profitable. Traders noted a few arbitrage sell programs had been triggered during bouts of weakness in the futures contract.

At settlement, March S&P 500s were up 6.80 points at 778.30, NASDAQ 100s rose 1.50 to 901.00, Russell 2000s rose 2.00 point to 370.00, Value Line futures were up 3.65 points to 703.45, Nikkei 225 index futures gained 570.0 to 18,350.0 and Midcap 400s rose 0.95 point to 263.70.
